title: Representation of arbitrary rational functions and polynomials by non-Foster resistor-capacitor-inductor networks
summary: The Bott-Duffin theorem shows that any arbitrary positive real rational function of finite order, representing a passive network, can be represented by a finite number of positive value resistors, capacitors and inductors. It is shown here that if the positivity restriction is lifted, any rational function or polynomial of any order may be represented by a network of (possibly negative) inductors, capacitors and resistors.
